page: Google Cloud Platform a2-megagpu-16g is an accelerator-optimized virtual machine tailored for extreme deep learning, high-performance computing, and large-scale parallel processing. The server is powered by 16 NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs providing a combined total of 640 GB of VRAM. The host compute platform features 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores with 2 threads per core) driven by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz. CPU cache levels consist of 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 38 MB L3 cache. Memory provisioning is substantial, featuring 1360.0 GB of system RAM, which provides 14.17 GB of system memory per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, requiring network-attached persistent storage for data persistence, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark data reflects the instance's high degree of parallelism alongside modest single-core execution characteristics. Multi-core performance is robust, highlighted by a strong top-25% result in stress-ng multi-core testing at 75,765.96 and strong performance in the PassMark CPU extended instructions test at 64,980.92, supported by AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI vector instruction sets. System memory throughput is similarly high-tier, registering 4,205.12 GB/sec for small-block cached reads and 193.62 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Conversely, the 2.2 GHz clock rate limits single-threaded throughput, resulting in bottom-25% rankings for stress-ng single-core (1,200.98), Geekbench single-core (1,046.0), single-threaded gzip compression (20.4 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (7.97 GB/sec).

In terms of qualitative resource efficiency, the a2-megagpu-16g delivers massive computational density by coupling 16 high-end accelerators with over a terabyte of RAM in a single instance. However, instances that prioritize accelerator throughput operate with higher base resource commitments, making them inefficient for workloads bottlenecked by single-thread frequency, modest data sets, or standard serial processing tasks. The absence of local NVMe storage also introduces a performance trade-off, shifting I/O dependencies entirely to remote network storage.

The a2-megagpu-16g is structured specifically for massive multi-GPU workloads. Key target applications include distributed large language model training, large-scale deep learning model inference, distributed ray tracing, complex physical simulations, and intensive data parallel ETL pipelines that can fully leverage 16 A100 GPUs and high system memory bandwidth.
description: Google Cloud Platform a2-megagpu-16g is an accelerator-optimized instance configured with 16 NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs delivering 640 GB of total VRAM. The system is backed by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor offering 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) running at 2.2 GHz, paired with 1360.0 GB of system RAM. The instance lacks bundled local storage and public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark performance shows strong multi-threaded execution and high memory read bandwidth (193.62 GB/sec uncached), reinforced by AVX-512 vector support, while single-core metrics remain in the bottom quartile due to base clock constraints. This dense hardware profile is engineered to eliminate multi-node communication bottlenecks in distributed deep learning training, massive AI inference, parallel ray tracing, and compute-heavy scientific simulations.
